fullName.value: Tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 2

texts.value: Cytokine that binds to TNFRSF1A/TNFR1 and TNFRSF1B/TNFBR, activating the tumor necrosis factor-mediated (TNF) signaling pathway (PubMed:33495441, PubMed:8395024). The TNF signaling pathway acts as a master regulator of the immune system, which either (1) promotes cell survival and inflammation by activating the canonical NF-kappa-B pathway or (2) trigger programmed cell death (apoptosis and necroptosis) (By similarity). Impairs regulatory T-cells (Treg) function in individuals with rheumatoid arthritis via FOXP3 dephosphorylation: acts by up-regulating the expression of protein phosphatase 1 (PP1), which dephosphorylates the key 'Ser-418' residue of FOXP3, thereby inactivating FOXP3 and rendering Treg cells functionally defective (By similarity). Key mediator of cell death in the anticancer action of BCG-stimulated neutrophils in combination with DIABLO/SMAC mimetic in the RT4v6 bladder cancer cell line (By similarity). Induces insulin resistance in adipocytes via inhibition of insulin-induced IRS1 tyrosine phosphorylation and insulin-induced glucose uptake (PubMed:25586176). Induces GKAP42 protein degradation in adipocytes which is partially responsible for TNF-induced insulin resistance (PubMed:25586176). Plays a role in angiogenesis by inducing VEGF production synergistically with IL1B and IL6 (By similarity). Promotes osteoclastogenesis and therefore mediates bone resorption (PubMed:32741026)

Cytokine mainly secreted by macrophages that binds to TNFRSF1A/TNFR1 and TNFRSF1B/TNFBR, activating the tumor necrosis factor-mediated (TNF) signaling pathway (PubMed:33495441, PubMed:8395024). The TNF signaling pathway acts as a master regulator of the immune system, which either (1) promotes cell survival and inflammation by activating the canonical NF-kappa-B pathway or (2) trigger programmed cell death (apoptosis and necroptosis) (By similarity)
The TNF intracellular domain (ICD) form induces IL12 production in dendritic cells
The TNF intracellular domain (ICD) form induces IL12 production in dendritic cells
Homotrimer

The soluble form derives from the membrane form by proteolytic processing by ADAM17. The membrane-bound form is further proteolytically processed by SPPL2A or SPPL2B through regulated intramembrane proteolysis producing TNF intracellular domains (ICD1 and ICD2) released in the cytosol and TNF C-domain 1 and C-domain 2 secreted into the extracellular space
The membrane form, but not the soluble form, is phosphorylated on serine residues. Dephosphorylation of the membrane form occurs by binding to soluble TNFRSF1A/TNFR1
O-glycosylated; glycans contain galactose, N-acetylgalactosamine and N-acetylneuraminic acid
The soluble form is demyristoylated by SIRT6, promoting its secretion

Mice develop normally without apparent phenotypic abnormalities, but display significant immune system and metabolic defects (PubMed:8395024, PubMed:8879212). Mutant mice show normal lymph node development but completely lack primary B cell follicles in the spleen, cannot form organized germinal centers, and exhibit compromised resistance to specific intracellular pathogens, such as L.monocytogenes (PubMed:8395024, PubMed:8879212)
Belongs to the tumor necrosis factor family

texts.value: Cytokine that binds to TNFRSF1A/TNFR1 and TNFRSF1B/TNFBR. It is mainly secreted by macrophages and can induce cell death of certain tumor cell lines. It is potent pyrogen causing fever by direct action or by stimulation of interleukin-1 secretion and is implicated in the induction of cachexia, Under certain conditions it can stimulate cell proliferation and induce cell differentiation. Induces insulin resistance in adipocytes via inhibition of insulin-induced IRS1 tyrosine phosphorylation and insulin-induced glucose uptake. Induces GKAP42 protein degradation in adipocytes which is partially responsible for TNF-induced insulin resistance. Plays a role in angiogenesis by inducing VEGF production synergistically with IL1B and IL6

The membrane-bound form is further proteolytically processed by SPPL2A or SPPL2B through regulated intramembrane proteolysis producing TNF intracellular domains (ICD1 and ICD2) released in the cytosol and TNF C-domain 1 and C-domain 2 secreted into the extracellular space
